clues: This small town sits on a small river in a flat plain by the sea. The land is low, and a big river is near.
Summers here are hot and humid, with about 25 days a year topping 90 degrees. Quick, heavy thunderstorms roll through in summer.
In 1777, the state moved its seat here from an old port town. It sat in the heart of the state, safe from British raids.
The fire crew in this town is made up of volunteers. It is the one state capital in the land with such a crew.
The governor of Delaware works in this city. The state's lawmakers meet here to make its laws.
